category_title: Students with ASD who initially engage through physical/sensory exploration and develop joint attention
minimal_context: The student is interacting with a dog in the school dinner hall while the teacher facilitates the session.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We have a little more time left in the dinner hall. Let's keep playing with the dog.

STUDENT: (Looks up to make eye contact, checking to see that you are watching his interactions with the dog, and makes a meaningful vocalization.)

TUTOR: Good job. Keep petting him.

STUDENT: (Appears focused and calm, sharing pleasure with you while continuing to interact with the dog.)

TUTOR: What else can you do with the dog? Keep playing.

STUDENT: (Suddenly switches off from his interactions with the dog, turning away to play alone and engage in repetitive sensory and ritualistic behaviors, almost as if he had 'had enough'.)

options.A: Allows the student to choose how to structure and use the dog interaction sessions.
options.B: Reviews a behavior tracking sheet with the student and has him count his positive and negative marks.
options.C: Maintains a complete absence of direct intervention during the dog interaction sessions.
options.D: Uses structured game activities to create a positive attitude about the dog interaction sessions.
